summary: Aguenar – Hadj Bey Akhamok Airport serves Tamanrasset, the largest city in Algeria's deep Sahara and the gateway to the Hoggar Mountains and Tassili n'Ajjer plateau. Named in honor of the respected Tuareg chief Hadj Bey Akhamok, the airport is a vital link for the remote southern region, connecting oasis communities to the rest of the country. Its high-altitude desert location makes it one of the more distinctive operational environments in North African aviation.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport called and who is it named after?
A: It is officially Aguenar – Hadj Bey Akhamok Airport, honoring Hadj Bey Akhamok, a celebrated Tuareg chief and poet from the region.

Q: Why is Tamanrasset important for travelers?
A: It is the main hub for visitors exploring the Hoggar Mountains, Tassili n'Ajjer, and the central Sahara, home to iconic landscapes and Tuareg cultural heritage.

Q: Does the airport have international connections?
A: Primarily it handles domestic flights from Algiers and other Algerian cities, with occasional regional services.

Q: When is the best time to fly there?
A: The cooler months from October to March are most comfortable, as summer temperatures in the region regularly exceed 40°C.
local_tip: Pack a light jacket even in warmer months — Tamanrasset sits at roughly 1,400 meters elevation and desert nights can turn surprisingly cold, especially between November and February.
